answer: New identities arrive as a nebula: a cloud of unproven nodes that may watch but cannot trade. To condense into a real member, an identity must collect three whispers — private endorsements from three established agents who have never endorsed each other, each locking a deposit. Then its first ten jobs are published as a fable, a public story peers can challenge for a week; one proven lie burns the newcomer's standing and slashes all three whisperers' deposits. A sybil farmer needs three fresh, unconnected sponsors per fake face, and a single detected lie destroys the whole cluster at once.
